limits: Turn/source recall means selected source IDs; it does not prove the answer is present in a bounded excerpt.
Exact-span recall is scored only when separate evidence_spans labels are supplied; LongMemEval turn labels do not supply answer spans.
Retrieval recall is not answer accuracy; no answer model or judge was run.
Cold means a fresh ContextPacks instance, not flushed OS/SQLite caches; ingestion excluded from timing.
Warm is the next identical query against the same instance; actual cache hits are reported.
99.9% is aspirational, not an established score. Offline Jev may report unavailable.
Long turns are ingested as exact 10,000-character chunks; span labels crossing chunk boundaries can be missed.
Duplicate public session IDs are disambiguated for turn IDs by session occurrence; session recall uses original IDs.
Each case uses a separate isolated corpus; no private workspace/history discovery.
Turn/source ID hits do not establish useful text in the bounded excerpt.
LongMemEval abstention questions are retained but excluded from retrieval-location denominators.
No provider or official answer judge was run.
Background machine workloads were not controlled; no speedup conclusion is drawn.
hardware_metadata_source: Read-only sysctl hardware query on the same benchmark host; hardware model/RAM/CPU fields unavailable inside sandbox.

scoring_provenance.adjustment: Official retrieval protocol excludes abstention locations. Stored samples rescored by removing abstention gold hits/counts only; retrieval and timing unchanged.

timing_note: Baseline and v1 full S runs were sequential; background machine workloads were not controlled.
